title: Virgo Filaments VII: MeerKAT HI-imaging of the VirgoIII filament
comment: 14 pages, 12 main figures (34 pages including appendices). Accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: We present MeerKAT HI observations of galaxies in the nearby Virgo III filament. At a median distance of $\sim30$ Mpc, the filament extends over $\approx16$ Mpc across $\sim56$ deg$^2$. Our survey comprises 15 targeted MeerKAT pointings centred on HI deficient galaxies. Multi-resolution HI imaging at 8-90 arcsec with an rms of $\sim0.3$ mJy beam$^{-1}$ reaches column densities of $\sim4\times10^{20}$ to $\sim4\times10^{18}$ atoms cm$^{-2}$. This probes HI in galaxy discs at $\sim1.2$ kpc resolution and their outskirts at $\sim13.5$ kpc. We detect HI emission from 80 sources within the 500-3000 km/s range; most are optically detected galaxies, while 10 per cent lack confirmed counterparts. We also identify three HI clouds without optical counterparts near an interacting system, possibly displaced during the interaction. Galaxies in the filament lie below the field HI gas-fraction scaling relations at fixed stellar mass. Crucially, $\sim40$ per cent of galaxies not selected for HI deficiency fall more than $1σ$ below these relations, with an even greater fraction lying under the mean relation itself, indicating that the low HI gas fractions are widespread in the filament rather than confined to the pre-selected deficient population. Quantifying HI morphologies using an asymmetry parameter, we find a wide range of disturbances without a clear trend with projected distance to the filament spine or local density, suggesting a combination of local interactions and the filament itself. This paper presents the survey description, catalogue, and HI atlas enabling investigations of gas removal mechanisms in Virgo III galaxies.

AI.tldr: MeerKAT HI survey of the Virgo III filament reveals widespread HI deficiency across the galaxy population, with disturbed morphologies suggesting combined local and filamentary effects.
AI.motivation: Galaxies in the Virgo III filament lie below field HI gas-fraction scaling relations, and the study aims to determine whether low HI content is confined to pre-selected HI-deficient galaxies or is widespread, and to investigate gas removal mechanisms in this large-scale structure environment.
AI.method: 15 targeted MeerKAT pointings centred on HI-deficient galaxies at median distance ~30 Mpc, covering ~16 Mpc across ~56 deg^2. Multi-resolution HI imaging (8-90 arcsec, rms ~0.3 mJy/beam) reaches column densities ~4e20 to ~4e18 atoms/cm^2, probing discs at ~1.2 kpc and outskirts at ~13.5 kpc resolution. HI morphologies quantified via an asymmetry parameter.
AI.result: HI emission detected from 80 sources (500-3000 km/s), mostly optically detected galaxies, with ~10 per cent lacking confirmed counterparts. Three HI clouds without optical counterparts found near an interacting system, possibly displaced during interaction. Galaxies lie below field HI gas-fraction scaling relations at fixed stellar mass; ~40 per cent of galaxies not pre-selected for HI deficiency fall more than 1 sigma below these relations, with even more below the mean. HI morphologies show a wide range of disturbances with no clear trend with projected distance to the filament spine or local density.
AI.conclusion: Low HI gas fractions are widespread in the Virgo III filament rather than confined to the pre-selected deficient population. Disturbed HI morphologies without clear dependence on filament position or density suggest a combination of local interactions and the filament environment as drivers. The paper provides the survey description, catalogue, and HI atlas for investigating gas removal mechanisms in Virgo III galaxies.

title: A Spectral Framework for Testing the Quasi-Star Hypothesis in Little Red Dots I: Weighing LRDs by Their Super-Eddington Luminosity Ratios---No Signs of Overmassive Black Holes
comment: 29 pages, 13 figures, 4 tables, submitted to ApJ
summary: We present a spectral test of the quasi-star hypothesis for Little Red Dots (LRDs) whereby a black hole grows inside a stellar-like envelope. We use \texttt{Prospector} to fit host galaxies and \texttt{TLUSTY} photospheres to four LRDs that show strong molecular or atomic absorption. We approximate each object's electron-scattered Eddington luminosity ratio, $φ\equiv κ_{\rm es}σT_{\rm eff}^{4}/(gc)$, and we use \texttt{MESA-QUEST} to simulate their envelopes. All four are super-Eddington at $φ= 4.0$--$299$, although the largest value sits at the edge of our atmosphere grid and beyond our simulations. We derive envelope masses between $700$--$27{,}000\,M_\odot$, where quasi-star theory requires the black hole to be less than a third of that. GN-28074 falls five decades below its published virial mass estimate, alleviating the overmassive black hole problem. Their black holes double in mass every $\sim0.05$--$3.5$~Myr and can produce intermediate-mass black holes in $\lesssim30$~Myr. The two fitted components of the water-absorbing object WIDE-EGS-2974 share a single $φ$, consistent with our hypothesis that the absorption originates in an extended atmosphere. We then extend our measurements to 82 archival LRDs, finding super-Eddington photospheres throughout the population that launch winds at $1$--$3\times$ their own escape speeds, which implies that LRDs evolve from being massive, continuum-driven sources to more eruptive winds as they mature and shed their outer envelopes. We thus constrain the Eddington ratios and masses of LRDs, and, for the first time, show self-consistently that quasi-stars may be the central engines powering LRDs.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a spectral test of the quasi-star hypothesis for Little Red Dots (LRDs), finding super-Eddington photospheres throughout the population and showing self-consistently that quasi-stars may be the central engines powering LRDs.
AI.motivation: The quasi-star hypothesis (a black hole growing inside a stellar-like envelope) has been proposed for LRDs, but lacked a self-consistent spectral test. The overmassive black hole problem and the unknown central engines of LRDs motivate constraining their Eddington ratios and masses.
AI.method: The authors use Prospector to fit host galaxies and TLUSTY photospheres to four LRDs showing strong molecular/atomic absorption. They approximate each object's electron-scattered Eddington luminosity ratio φ ≡ κ_es σ T_eff^4/(gc) and use MESA-QUEST to simulate their envelopes. They then extend measurements to 82 archival LRDs.
AI.result: All four LRDs are super-Eddington at φ = 4.0–299. Envelope masses range from 700 to 27,000 M_⊙. GN-28074 falls five decades below its published virial mass estimate. Black holes double in mass every ~0.05–3.5 Myr and can produce intermediate-mass black holes in ≲30 Myr. The two fitted components of water-absorbing WIDE-EGS-2974 share a single φ. Across 82 archival LRDs, super-Eddington photospheres launch winds at 1–3× their escape speeds.
AI.conclusion: The results constrain Eddington ratios and masses of LRDs and, for the first time, show self-consistently that quasi-stars may be the central engines powering LRDs. LRDs appear to evolve from massive, continuum-driven sources to more eruptive winds as they mature and shed outer envelopes.

title: SHELLQs. Black Hole Mass and Eddington Ratio Distributions of Intermediate-Luminosity Quasars at 6<z<7
comment: 36 pages, 16 figures, submitted to ApJ
summary: We present near-infrared spectroscopy of 21 quasars at 6.07 < z < 6.90 obtained with JWST/NIRSpec and Subaru/MOIRCS. These targets have absolute ultraviolet magnitudes of -25 < M_1450 < -22 and are drawn from a sample of z>6 quasars identified in the Subaru High-z Exploration of Low-Luminosity Quasars (SHELLQs) project. These quasars occupy the intermediate-luminosity regime between luminous quasars and the faint high-redshift AGNs uncovered by JWST. We detect broad Balmer emission lines and MgII 2798 with underlying continua from the NIRSpec and MOIRCS targets, respectively. The virial black hole masses of this sample span a wide range of 7.2 < log M_BH/M_sun < 9.4, with Eddington ratios of -1.3 < log L_bol/L_Edd < 0.4. Combining these measurements with our previous mass estimates for other SHELLQs quasars, we construct a sample of 27 quasars with M_BH estimates at 6 < z < 7 and derive the distributions of M_BH and L_bol/L_Edd. When compared with luminosity-matched quasars at z ~ 1.3, we find median offsets of delta log M_BH/M_sun = -0.4 and Delta log L_bol/L_Edd = 0.2 in the high-redshift sample. In addition, 11% of the high-redshift quasars are accreting near or above the Eddington limit. As a systematic check, adopting the Eddington-ratio-dependent calibration of single-epoch M_BH estimates increases the inferred super-Eddington fraction to 22%. These results indicate that a representative population of distant supermassive black holes undergo a rapid accretion phase, although not as extreme as that seen in the most luminous quasar population, consistent with the anti-hierarchical growth scenario of supermassive black holes.

AI.tldr: Near-IR spectroscopy of 21 intermediate-luminosity z>6 quasars yields virial black hole masses and Eddington ratios, revealing rapid accretion consistent with anti-hierarchical supermassive black hole growth.
AI.motivation: The intermediate-luminosity regime between luminous quasars and faint JWST AGNs at z>6 is poorly constrained, leaving unclear whether a representative distant black hole population undergoes rapid accretion or only the most luminous extreme.
AI.method: JWST/NIRSpec and Subaru/MOIRCS near-infrared spectroscopy of 21 SHELLQs quasars at 6.07<z<6.90 (-25<M_1450<-22). Broad Balmer lines and MgII 2798 with continua are used for single-epoch virial black hole masses; combined with previous SHELLQs estimates to form a 27-quasar sample at 6<z<7, compared to luminosity-matched z~1.3 quasars, with an Eddington-ratio-dependent calibration as systematic check.
AI.result: Virial black hole masses span 7.2<log M_BH/M_sun<9.4 with Eddington ratios -1.3<log L_bol/L_Edd<0.4. Relative to z~1.3 matched quasars, median offsets are delta log M_BH/M_sun=-0.4 and Delta log L_bol/L_Edd=0.2. About 11% accrete near or above Eddington, rising to 22% under the Eddington-ratio-dependent calibration.
AI.conclusion: A representative population of distant supermassive black holes undergoes a rapid accretion phase, though not as extreme as the most luminous quasars, consistent with anti-hierarchical black hole growth.

title: RIGEL: Ultra-faint dwarf galaxy diversity shaped by inhomogeneous cosmic reionization
comment: 18 pages, 14 figures, submitted to A&A
summary: Ultra-faint dwarf galaxies (UFDs) are among the smallest and oldest galaxies in the Universe and are widely regarded as relics of cosmic reionization. To investigate how reionization quenches star formation and shapes the diversity of UFDs, we present a suite of eight cosmological zoom-in simulations of isolated UFDs with present-day halo masses of $\sim10^9\,{\rm M}_\odot$. The simulations are performed with the radiation-magnetohydrodynamic galaxy formation framework Realistic ISM modeling in Galaxy Evolution and Lifecycles (RIGEL), coupled to realistic large-scale radiation fields extracted from the THESAN reionization simulation. Despite residing in similar $z=0$ halos, the simulated galaxies span nearly two orders of magnitude in stellar mass and broadly reproduce the observed luminosities, sizes, metallicities, and stellar kinematics of Local Group UFDs. We find that reionization quenches star formation through a two-stage process. The arrival of the ionization front rapidly photoionizes the diffuse circumgalactic and intergalactic gas, suppressing further gas accretion onto the galaxy. Star formation nevertheless continues for several hundred Myr using the surviving self-shielded gas reservoir and ceases only after this gas is consumed or dispersed. Within 500 Myr after reionization, less than 40% of the initial gas mass remains in the halo, with photoevaporation constituting the dominant gas-loss channel. We further show that the halo mass at the time of reionization is a key parameter governing the subsequent evolution of UFDs. Galaxies residing in more massive halos at reionization retain gas for longer periods and undergo more extended chemical enrichment. Consequently, the halo mass at reionization strongly correlates with the final stellar mass, stellar age spread, and chemical evolution of the galaxy.

AI.tldr: Cosmological zoom-in simulations with RIGEL and THESAN radiation fields show that reionization quenches ultra-faint dwarf galaxies in two stages: rapid suppression of gas accretion followed by delayed cessation of star formation once self-shielded gas is consumed, with halo mass at reionization governing final stellar mass and chemical evolution.
AI.motivation: Ultra-faint dwarf galaxies (UFDs) are among the smallest and oldest galaxies and are considered relics of cosmic reionization, but how reionization quenches star formation and drives the diversity of UFDs remains unclear.
AI.method: Eight cosmological zoom-in simulations of isolated UFDs with present-day halo masses of ~1e9 solar masses, run with the radiation-magnetohydrodynamic galaxy formation framework RIGEL coupled to realistic large-scale radiation fields extracted from the THESAN reionization simulation.
AI.result: Despite similar z=0 halos, the simulated galaxies span nearly two orders of magnitude in stellar mass and broadly reproduce observed luminosities, sizes, metallicities, and stellar kinematics of Local Group UFDs. Reionization quenches star formation in two stages: the ionization front photoionizes diffuse circumgalactic and intergalactic gas, suppressing accretion; star formation continues for several hundred Myr from surviving self-shielded gas and stops once it is consumed or dispersed. Within 500 Myr after reionization, less than 40% of the initial gas mass remains, with photoevaporation dominating gas loss.
AI.conclusion: Halo mass at the time of reionization is a key parameter controlling UFD evolution: galaxies in more massive halos retain gas longer and experience more extended chemical enrichment, so this halo mass strongly correlates with the final stellar mass, stellar age spread, and chemical evolution of the galaxy.

title: Chromospheric and Transition Region Responses of activities at the base of Coronal Plumes
comment: 19 pages, 11 figures, 1 table. Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: We present the identification of the co-spatial and co-temporal small scale jets -- sometimes also named as jetlets -- at the base of the coronal hole plume associated with chromospheric and transition region (TR) flows. We identified 19 jets with coordinated observations recorded on March 19, 2016 using the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) and the Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph (IRIS). Our analysis of \ion{Si}{4} 1393.7~Å line suggests blueshifts mostly in the range of 10 to 33~km~s$^{-1}$, but few less than -10~km~s$^{-1}$, while analysis of co-spatial \ion{Mg}{2}~h~\&~k lines show both blueshifts and redshifts in the range of {--}9 to 17~km~s$^{-1}$. We observed highly asymmetric, enhanced intensity in \ion{Si}{4} line during these events. The upflows observed in transition region through \ion{Si}{4} is strongly correlated with chromospheric downflows observed in \ion{Mg}{2}. We interpret these results as a signature of interchange reconnections creating bi-directional flows -- giving rise to upflows (downflows) in transition region (chromosphere).

AI.tldr: Nineteen small-scale jets (jetlets) at the base of a coronal hole plume were identified using coordinated SDO and IRIS observations, revealing bi-directional flows consistent with interchange reconnection.
AI.motivation: Small-scale jets at the base of coronal hole plumes are poorly characterized, particularly their relationship to chromospheric and transition region flows. Understanding these events could clarify how interchange reconnection drives mass and energy transport in the low solar atmosphere.
AI.method: The authors analyzed coordinated observations from March 19, 2016, using SDO and IRIS to identify 19 co-spatial and co-temporal jetlets at the base of a coronal hole plume. They measured Doppler shifts in the Si IV 1393.7 Å and Mg II h & k lines to characterize plasma flows.
AI.result: Si IV 1393.7 Å showed blueshifts mostly between 10 and 33 km/s, with a few below -10 km/s, while co-spatial Mg II h & k lines showed both blueshifts and redshifts ranging from -9 to 17 km/s. The Si IV line exhibited highly asymmetric, enhanced intensity during the events, and upflows in the transition region were strongly correlated with chromospheric downflows in Mg II.
AI.conclusion: The observed bi-directional flows—transition region upflows coupled with chromospheric downflows—are interpreted as signatures of interchange reconnection generating these flows at the base of the coronal hole plume.

title: The Ashes of Supermassive Stars: Globular Cluster-like Aluminum Enhancement in Little Red Dots
comment: Submitted. 19 pages. 14 figures. 2 tables
summary: The relative abundances of elements in galaxies serve as fossil records of the physical conditions and processes by which they were forged. While the Big Bang produced only the lightest elements, subsequent stellar nucleosynthesis imprinted characteristic abundance patterns onto the surrounding gas, set initially by the temperatures reached inside stars and subsequently shaped by how the processed material was mixed and released. Globular clusters - dense, ancient groups of stars - provide a striking unique example. Some contain stars depleted in magnesium and enriched in aluminum, showing that they formed from gas exposed to exceptionally hot hydrogen burning. The stars responsible remain unknown. Little Red Dots may provide this missing engine. These compact, luminous objects formed at cosmic epochs similar to those associated with globular-cluster formation and are enshrouded by dense gas whose chemical composition can be measured with the James Webb Space Telescope. Here, using deep spectroscopy from the SPURS program, we show that this abundance pattern characterizes the LRD central engine: magnesium-depleted and aluminum-enhanced gas with a metallicity only 1% that of the Sun. This pattern is not produced by ordinary massive stars at these redshifts and cannot be mimicked by ionization, gas geometry or dust. Instead, it is reproduced by hot hydrogen burning in fully convective supermassive stars, with the measured abundances implying masses of at least 10,000 solar masses - approximately 100 times larger than any star observed in the present-day Universe. Little Red Dots may therefore reveal supermassive stars during their brief lives or in the immediate aftermath of their direct collapse, simultaneously identifying the long-sought source of globular cluster abundance anomalies and a formation pathway for massive black hole seeds.

AI.tldr: Deep JWST/SPURS spectroscopy shows that Little Red Dots host gas with a Mg-depleted, Al-enhanced abundance pattern at 1% solar metallicity, a signature reproduced by hot hydrogen burning in fully convective supermassive stars (≥10,000 M☉), thereby linking these objects to globular cluster abundance anomalies and massive black hole seed formation.
AI.motivation: Elemental abundances in galaxies are fossil records of the physical conditions and processes of their formation. Globular clusters contain stars depleted in magnesium and enriched in aluminum, indicating formation from gas exposed to exceptionally hot hydrogen burning, yet the responsible stellar source has remained unknown. Little Red Dots, compact luminous objects from cosmic epochs similar to globular cluster formation and enshrouded in dense gas, are proposed as this missing engine.
AI.method: The authors used deep spectroscopy from the SPURS program with the James Webb Space Telescope to measure the chemical composition of the dense gas enshrouding Little Red Dots. They tested whether the observed abundance pattern could arise from ordinary massive stars, ionization, gas geometry, or dust, and compared it to nucleosynthetic predictions for hot hydrogen burning in fully convective supermassive stars.
AI.result: The LRD central engine exhibits a magnesium-depleted, aluminum-enhanced abundance pattern with a metallicity only 1% that of the Sun. This pattern is not produced by ordinary massive stars at these redshifts and cannot be mimicked by ionization, gas geometry, or dust. It is instead reproduced by hot hydrogen burning in fully convective supermassive stars, with the measured abundances implying masses of at least 10,000 solar masses, approximately 100 times larger than any star observed in the present-day Universe.
AI.conclusion: Little Red Dots may reveal supermassive stars during their brief lives or in the immediate aftermath of their direct collapse, simultaneously identifying the long-sought source of globular cluster abundance anomalies and a formation pathway for massive black hole seeds.

title: Cycle Variation in the Occurrence of Great Soft X-ray Solar Flares
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures. Accepted by Solar Physics, 2026
summary: Powerful nonstationary processes such as flares and coronal mass ejections are detected mainly near the solar cycle maxima. However, the analysis of the great flares since 1975, when the GOES monitoring started, leads us to more precise conclusions. We have traced the latitudinal distribution of X-class flares and their dependence on the phase of the cycle throughout four cycles. Besides, we compared directly their positions with the magnetic field structure. It was found that the relatively weak X4--7 flares occur at relatively high latitudes (15 -- 20 degrees), where two waves of activity converge, one moving toward the equator and the other, the wave of the following cycle, directed poleward. Such events are observed almost constantly 1 -- 2 years before the cycle maximum. At the same time, the number of the powerful X-ray flares increases sharply during the maximum phase, but the greatest X10 flares are observed at the beginning of the decline phase, where wave interactions still persist, and throughout the decline phase. Note that they are virtually absent during the cycle growth phase. Thus, we conclude that the greatest X-ray flares begin to appear 1 -- 2 years before the maximum number of sunspots in the overlapping phase, when different kinds of activity waves coexist on the Sun at relatively high latitudes, and, then, continue to appear at the boundary, which separates the wave of local fields and the poleward wave of the following cycle.

AI.tldr: X-class solar flares show distinct latitudinal and cycle-phase dependence: X4–7 flares occur at high latitudes during the overlapping phase before cycle maximum, while the greatest X10 flares appear from the early decline phase, when waves of different cycles coexist.
AI.motivation: Flares and coronal mass ejections are thought to occur mainly near solar cycle maxima, but this coarse view is imprecise. The study aims to refine this picture by examining how the latitudinal distribution and timing of the most powerful X-class flares relate to the phase of the solar cycle and to the underlying magnetic field structure.
AI.method: Using GOES X-ray monitoring data since 1975 (four solar cycles), the authors traced the latitudinal positions of X-class flares and their dependence on cycle phase. They directly compared flare locations with the magnetic field structure, focusing on wave interactions between the equatorward wave of the current cycle and the poleward wave of the following cycle.
AI.result: Relatively weak X4–7 flares occur at relatively high latitudes (15–20°), where an equatorward wave and the poleward wave of the following cycle converge; these are observed almost continuously 1–2 years before cycle maximum. Powerful X-ray flares increase sharply during maximum, but the greatest X10 flares occur at the beginning of and throughout the decline phase, where wave interactions persist, and are virtually absent during the cycle growth phase.
AI.conclusion: The greatest X-ray flares begin to appear 1–2 years before the maximum sunspot number, in the overlapping phase when different activity waves coexist at relatively high solar latitudes, and continue to appear at the boundary separating the wave of local fields from the poleward wave of the following cycle.

title: Overmassive No More: The Case for Little Red Dots Hosting Black Hole Seeds as Massive as Single Supermassive Stars
comment: Submitted to the Open Journal of Astrophysics. Main results in Figs. 6 (HR diagram), 7 (non-virial vs. virial BH* masses), and 8 (non-virial BH* masses below SMS mass ceiling). Comments warmly welcomed!
summary: Little Red Dots (LRDs) display singular properties unlike any known class of AGN or galaxies, motivating novel mass estimators for their central engines. Inspired by their similarities to stellar phenomena, here we interpret the LRD continuum as being produced by a pseudo-photosphere. We fit tailored stellar atmosphere models to host-subtracted LRD central engines ("black hole stars," BH*s) represented by stacks of $117$ objects. Typical BH* continuum spectra are well fit by models in a narrow range of temperatures ($T_{\rm eff}\approx4200-4800$ K), with bolometric luminosities $\approx10^{43-45}$ erg s$^{-1}$, implying pseudo-photospheric radii $\approx700-2000$ au. Based on these parameters, we explore four different approaches to deriving BH* masses: 1) using the surface gravity from atmosphere models; 2) appealing to the resemblance to super-Eddington phenomena; 3) approximating the escape velocity from the outflowing material; and 4) exploiting the lack of variability to bound the dynamical time. For the typical BH*, all of these methods yield remarkably consistent masses of $\approx10^{4-5}\,M_\odot$, implying a highly super-Eddington luminosity of $L_{\rm{bol}}/L_{\rm{Edd}}\sim5-50$. These mass estimates place BH*s within the scatter of the local scaling relation between black hole mass and host galaxy stellar mass, providing a self-consistent alternative to "overmassive" black holes that lie $2-3$ dex above it. Crucially, our derived masses are consistent with BH*s arising from single supermassive stars (SMSs), whose masses cannot exceed $\approx10^{5-6}\,M_\odot$ due to general relativistic instabilities. Furthermore, for our derived $L_{\rm bol}/L_{\rm Edd}$, the sharp cutoff of the LRD luminosity function matches the maximum theoretical mass of an SMS. With LRDs, we may therefore be directly observing the birth of heavy black hole seeds.

AI.tldr: LRD continua are modeled as pseudo-photospheres from "black hole stars," yielding consistent masses of ~10^4-5 M_sun, suggesting LRDs are the birth of heavy black hole seeds from supermassive stars.
AI.motivation: Little Red Dots (LRDs) have properties unlike any known AGN or galaxy class, motivating new mass estimators for their central engines. Their similarity to stellar phenomena suggests a pseudo-photosphere interpretation.
AI.method: Stellar atmosphere models were fit to host-subtracted LRD central engines ("black hole stars," BH*s) represented by stacks of 117 objects. Four independent approaches to BH* mass were explored: 1) surface gravity from atmosphere models; 2) resemblance to super-Eddington phenomena; 3) escape velocity from outflowing material; 4) lack of variability to bound dynamical time.
AI.result: Typical BH* continuum spectra are well fit by models with T_eff ~ 4200-4800 K, bolometric luminosities ~10^43-45 erg/s, and pseudo-photospheric radii ~700-2000 au. All four mass methods yield remarkably consistent masses ~10^4-5 M_sun, implying highly super-Eddington luminosity L_bol/L_Edd ~ 5-50.
AI.conclusion: The derived masses place BH*s within the scatter of the local black hole mass-host galaxy stellar mass scaling relation, providing a self-consistent alternative to "overmassive" black holes (which lie 2-3 dex above it). The masses are consistent with BH*s arising from single supermassive stars (SMSs) capped at ~10^5-6 M_sun by general relativistic instabilities, and for the derived L_bol/L_Edd the LRD luminosity function cutoff matches the maximum SMS mass. LRDs may thus be direct observations of the birth of heavy black hole seeds.

title: Planetary Nebula Central Stars as Tracers of Planetary Nebula-Star Cluster Associations in the Galaxy
comment: 19 pages, 2 figures
summary: Planetary nebulae (PNe) that are physically associated with star clusters are rare but crucial for stellar evolution studies because they allow their initial and final stellar properties to be determined independently, contributing to constraints on the initial-to-final-mass relation (IFMR), which traces stellar mass loss. Although the identification of such pairs is essential, most reported cases have been identified incidentally rather than through systematic searches. Here, we attempt to uncover new such associations in our Galaxy employing literature PN central stars (CSs) and star cluster catalogues. Exploring relevant angular positions on the sky and kinematic Gaia DR3 data, we identify 38 candidate CS-cluster pairs. The components of eight of these pairs present consistent interstellar extinctions, and their CS properties are compatible with stellar evolution models. Two of these candidate pairs are already reported in the literature as true associations. We evaluate separately the remaining six pairs using literature PN observational data, assessing the likelihood of each pair being a true association. The initial and final masses of our best candidates are mostly consistent with the latest IFMR predictions and confirmed cluster-PNe points. An additional 46 CS-cluster pairs have components with compatible angular positions but lack kinematic CS data and are thus presented separately. More data are needed for a precise estimation of the physical parameters of most of our candidates and to confirm these associations, which will be addressed in future studies.

AI.tldr: This study systematically searches for planetary nebulae physically associated with star clusters in the Galaxy, identifying 38 candidate central star-cluster pairs via literature PN central stars, star cluster catalogues, and Gaia DR3 kinematics.
AI.motivation: PNe physically associated with star clusters are rare but valuable for stellar evolution studies, as they independently constrain initial and final stellar properties, thus informing the initial-to-final-mass relation (IFMR). Most known pairs were found incidentally rather than through systematic searches, motivating a dedicated search.
AI.method: The authors cross-matched literature PN central stars (CSs) with star cluster catalogues, examining angular positions on the sky and kinematic Gaia DR3 data to identify candidate CS-cluster pairs. They screened candidates for consistent interstellar extinction and compatibility of CS properties with stellar evolution models, then evaluated the remaining pairs individually using literature PN observational data to assess the likelihood of true association.
AI.result: 38 candidate CS-cluster pairs were identified. Eight pairs show consistent interstellar extinctions and CS properties compatible with stellar evolution models; two of these are already reported as true associations in the literature. The remaining six were assessed individually. Initial and final masses of the best candidates are mostly consistent with the latest IFMR predictions and confirmed cluster-PNe points. An additional 46 CS-cluster pairs with compatible angular positions but lacking kinematic CS data are presented separately.
AI.conclusion: The search uncovered new candidate PN-cluster associations, with the best candidates supporting current IFMR predictions. However, more data are needed to precisely estimate physical parameters and confirm most candidates, which will be addressed in future studies.

title: Deus Ex Statistica: A Statistical Solution to the binary-binary Outcome of the Chaotic, Non-Hierarchical Four-Body Problem
comment: 11 pages, 8 figures
summary: We present an analytical, statistical solution to the binary-binary (2+2) outcome of the chaotic non-hierarchical four-body problem. The solution is based on the density-of-states formulation pioneered by J. J. Monaghan. The method skips the computationally expensive integration of the equations of motion, and instead samples the outcome from the chaotic phase-space, subject to conservation of energy, momentum, and angular momentum. From the joint distribution, we extract marginal distributions of several key parameters using Monte-Carlo integration, and numerically verify them by comparing to an identical ensemble of scattering experiments produced by the FEWBODY code. From the comparison, we identify a regime not represented by the density-of-states formulation: the hard binary regime, where one binary is much harder then the four-body energy scale, and the system acts as an effective three-body system. We hypothesize that at this regime the system's probability distribution spreads over an effective reduced three-body chaotic phase space. The process of transfer from four-body to three-body phase-space is still not understood, and represents the next natural extension of density-of-states methods.

AI.tldr: The paper derives an analytical, statistical solution to the binary-binary (2+2) outcome of the chaotic non-hierarchical four-body problem using Monaghan's density-of-states formulation, avoiding costly equation-of-motion integration. Marginal distributions are extracted via Monte-Carlo integration and validated against FEWBODY scattering experiments, revealing a "hard binary regime" not captured by the formulation.
AI.motivation: The chaotic non-hierarchical four-body problem's binary-binary outcome is computationally expensive to solve via direct integration of equations of motion. A faster, statistical approach is desired to sample outcomes from the chaotic phase space subject to conservation laws.
AI.method: The authors apply the density-of-states formulation pioneered by J. J. Monaghan, skipping the expensive integration of equations of motion and instead sampling outcomes from the chaotic phase space while respecting conservation of energy, momentum, and angular momentum. Marginal distributions of key parameters are extracted from the joint distribution using Monte-Carlo integration, then verified against an identical ensemble of scattering experiments produced by the FEWBODY code.
AI.result: The density-of-states predictions were compared to FEWBODY scattering experiments, revealing a regime not represented by the formulation: the hard binary regime, where one binary is much harder than the four-body energy scale and the system behaves as an effective three-body system.
AI.conclusion: The density-of-states formulation successfully provides an analytical, statistical solution to the binary-binary outcome but fails in the hard binary regime, where the system's probability distribution likely spreads over an effective reduced three-body chaotic phase space. The transfer process from four-body to three-body phase space remains unexplained and is identified as the next natural extension of density-of-states methods.

title: The FU Ori outburst of PR Ori B
comment: 23 pages, 16 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for publication at ApJ
summary: We report the discovery of a nearby FU Ori-type outburst (FUor), PR Ori B, in the L1641 cluster of the Orion star-forming region. The high-amplitude variability was first identified in the NEOWISE (3-5 $μ$m) photometry of the unresolved PR Ori binary system. Long-term, resolved optical photometric monitoring demonstrates that PR Ori B is the driver of a $ΔG=5~$mag outburst, while PR Ori A has remained constant over the last 20 years. The near-IR spectrum of PR Ori B changes from a late K-type spectral type during quiescence to a viscously heated disk during outburst, including deep absorption in $^{12}$CO and H$_2$O bands. The optical spectrum also exhibits features that are commonly associated with FUors, including P Cygni profiles in Na I D lines and absorption in the Ca II infrared triplet. The luminosity of the outburst (L$_{acc}\sim$30--40 L$_\odot$) is similar to that commonly observed in FUors. The comparison of Spitzer/IRS and VLT/VISIR spectroscopy shows some evidence of silicate crystallisation during the outburst. PR Ori B is one of the closest and brightest FUors discovered over the last few years, only one magnitude fainter than the archetype of the class FU Ori. The proximity and brightness will allow for future high angular resolution observations to probe the physics of the inner disk and to evaluate changes in the disk due to the increased luminosity.

AI.tldr: Discovery of PR Ori B, a nearby FU Ori-type outburst in the L1641 cluster of Orion, driven by one component of the PR Ori binary, exhibiting a 5 mag optical outburst with FUor-typical spectroscopic and accretion signatures.
AI.motivation: FUor outbursts are poorly understood in terms of inner-disk physics and disk response to rapid luminosity increases. A nearby, bright, well-resolved FUor enables high angular resolution follow-up, motivating the identification and characterization of such an object.
AI.method: NEOWISE (3-5 μm) photometry revealed high-amplitude variability in the unresolved PR Ori binary. Long-term resolved optical photometric monitoring identified PR Ori B as the outbursting component. Near-IR and optical spectroscopy characterized the spectral evolution, and Spitzer/IRS and VLT/VISIR spectroscopy probed dust properties.
AI.result: PR Ori B drives a ΔG=5 mag outburst while PR Ori A remains constant over 20 years. Its near-IR spectrum shifts from a late K-type quiescent type to a viscously heated disk in outburst with deep ¹²CO and H₂O absorption. Optical spectra show FUor-typical P Cygni Na I D profiles and Ca II infrared triplet absorption. Outburst luminosity L_acc ~30–40 L_sun. Spitzer/IRS vs. VLT/VISIR comparison suggests silicate crystallisation during outburst. It is one of the closest and brightest FUors found recently, only one magnitude fainter than FU Ori.
AI.conclusion: PR Ori B is a nearby, bright FUor ideal for future high angular resolution studies of inner-disk physics and luminosity-driven disk changes.

title: Chasing Cosmic Reionization: An Extremely Faint Highly Magnified Source at $z=5.66$ with high $ξ_{\rm ion}$
comment: Submitted to ApJL. 8 pages, 4 figures, 1 table
summary: We present JWST NIRSpec IFU spectroscopic measurements of one of the faintest (M$_{UV}>-13.6$) known ionizing sources at $z=5.66$, dubbed Small And Lensed Source Arc, SALSA. This source is highly magnified ($μ>100$) by the lensing galaxy cluster Abell 2744, providing a unique opportunity to investigate the physical properties of faint sources in the Epoch of Reionization. We characterize SALSA's nebular emission using rest-frame UV and optical emission lines and investigate the relationship between its ionizing efficiency, nebular excitation, and chemical enrichment. We robustly detect H$α$ emission and use it to predict the H$β$ flux assuming negligible dust attenuation. We also measure the [OIII]$λ$5007 emission and estimate oxygen abundance resulting in a high R3 index $2.82_{-0.25}^{+0.34}$ and relatively low metallicity $\mathrm{12+log(O/H)}= 7.43\pm0.09$. SALSA presents a high ionizing production efficiency log$(ξ_{ion})=25.49_{-0.08}^{+0.09}$ Hz erg $^{-1}$, consistent with theoretical models from very massive stars and constant star formation rate, and a high Ly$α$ escape fraction $f_{\mathrm{esc}}^{\mathrm{Ly}α}=0.39\pm0.14$. These properties place SALSA among the most extreme star-forming sources known at this epoch.

AI.tldr: JWST NIRSpec IFU spectroscopy of the faint, highly lensed ionizing source SALSA at z=5.66 reveals extreme star-formation properties, including a high R3 index, low metallicity, high ionizing production efficiency, and a high Lyα escape fraction.
AI.motivation: Faint ionizing sources during the Epoch of Reionization are difficult to study. Gravitational lensing offers a rare opportunity to probe the physical properties of such intrinsically faint objects at high redshift.
AI.method: JWST NIRSpec IFU spectroscopy of SALSA, magnified (μ>100) by the Abell 2744 cluster. The authors analyze rest-frame UV and optical emission lines, detect Hα, predict Hβ assuming negligible dust, measure [OIII]λ5007, and derive oxygen abundance, R3 index, ionizing efficiency, and Lyα escape fraction.
AI.result: SALSA shows a high R3 index of 2.82_{-0.25}^{+0.34}, low metallicity 12+log(O/H)=7.43±0.09, high ionizing production efficiency log(ξion)=25.49_{-0.08}^{+0.09} Hz erg^-1, consistent with very massive stars and constant star formation, and a high Lyα escape fraction f_esc^Lyα=0.39±0.14.
AI.conclusion: SALSA is among the most extreme known star-forming sources at z~5.66, providing insight into the physical properties and ionizing output of faint galaxies during the Epoch of Reionization.

title: Automated Detection of Double-Lined Spectroscopic Binaries in High-Resolution Spectra and a Probabilistic Analysis of Stellar Multiplicity
summary: The characterization of Sun-like stars, including determining whether those stars are single or have stellar companions, has become increasingly important for missions seeking planets beyond the Solar System. With upcoming missions like the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) on the horizon, vetting stars for binarity and confirming potential targets as viable is essential precursor science. In this paper, we present an automated algorithm that searches for double-lined spectroscopic binaries (SB2s) in high-resolution spectra. Using MOLUSC, we simulate realistic stellar populations to quantify the capability of algorithm for detecting stellar companions around nearby stars, with potential applications to HWO target stars and Gaia DR4 planet-host candidates. In addition, we explore how the detection rate is influenced by complementary observations like high-resolution adaptive optics imaging and time-series radial velocities. We find that our SB2 detection algorithm alone can rule out 46.1% of stellar-mass companions. High-resolution adaptive optics alone rules out 79.6% of stellar companions. Radial velocity surveys alone ruled out 98.4% and 98.7% for 5-year and 10-year surveys, respectively. When all three methods are combined, the probability of a typical nearby star having a stellar companion is <1%. The combination of the methods allows us to better understand and resolve target lists for future surveys.

AI.tldr: An automated SB2 search algorithm is presented and benchmarked via MOLUSC simulations, quantifying companion-detection completeness for nearby Sun-like stars and the gains from combining it with adaptive optics and radial velocity surveys.
AI.motivation: Upcoming exoplanet missions such as the Habitable Worlds Observatory require knowing whether candidate Sun-like target stars are single or have stellar companions; vetting binarity is essential precursor science for target selection and validation.
AI.method: An automated algorithm searches high-resolution spectra for double-lined spectroscopic binaries (SB2s). Using MOLUSC, realistic stellar populations are simulated to quantify companion-detection capability for nearby stars, relevant to HWO targets and Gaia DR4 planet-host candidates. The influence of complementary observations—high-resolution adaptive optics (AO) imaging and time-series radial velocities (RVs)—on detection rate is also explored.
AI.result: The SB2 algorithm alone rules out 46.1% of stellar-mass companions. High-resolution AO alone rules out 79.6%. RV surveys alone rule out 98.4% (5-year) and 98.7% (10-year). Combined, the probability that a typical nearby star has a stellar companion is <1%.
AI.conclusion: Combining SB2 detection, AO imaging, and RV surveys substantially improves binarity vetting, enabling better understanding and refinement of target lists for future exoplanet surveys.

title: Exploring the AGN population in protoclusters: results from the TNG300 simulation and comparison with observations
comment: 14 pages, 12 Figures, submitted to A&A
summary: In this work, we investigate the physical properties and cosmic evolution of galaxies and AGN in a sample of 280 protoclusters identified in the TNG300 simulation, selected to end up in $z = 0$ clusters with $M_{200, \rm c} > 10^{14} \, {\rm M_{\odot}}$. Our goal is to provide the first statistical view of AGN activity enhancement in a uniformly defined sample of overdense environments, and to identify the physical mechanisms driving it. We identify protoclusters as the progenitors of present-day galaxy clusters through merger-tree reconstruction and compare their galaxy and AGN populations with a control sample of field galaxies across the redshift range $0 \leq z \leq 6$. We investigate galaxy and SMBH demographics, AGN fractions, bolometric luminosity functions, and the SMBH accretion rate density, consistently applying homogeneous selection criteria in all environments. We find that TNG300 protoclusters host systematically more massive galaxies and SMBHs than the field by up to $1 \, {\rm dex}$ at all redshifts, with signatures of accelerated galaxy evolution already visible at $z \sim 3-4$. The AGN fraction increases with stellar mass in both environments and, at fixed host-galaxy stellar mass, is broadly consistent between protoclusters and field galaxies, indicating no strong environmental triggering of SMBH accretion. However, when analysed as a function of redshift, protoclusters exhibit a significant enhancement of AGN activity (by a factor $> 2$), particularly at high luminosities and early cosmic times. We show that this enhancement primarily arises from differences in the stellar-mass distributions of galaxies in overdense regions, where massive systems assemble earlier than in the field. Consistently, protoclusters dominate the bright end of the AGN bolometric luminosity function and contribute up to $\sim 50\%$ of the total SMBH accretion rate density at $z \sim 6$.

AI.tldr: Using 280 TNG300 protoclusters, the study finds that enhanced AGN activity in overdense regions is driven mainly by earlier assembly of massive galaxies rather than by environmental triggering of SMBH accretion.
AI.motivation: To provide the first statistical view of AGN activity enhancement in a uniformly defined sample of overdense environments and to identify the physical mechanisms driving it.
AI.method: 280 protoclusters in TNG300 (ending in z=0 clusters with M200,c > 1e14 Msun) identified via merger-tree reconstruction, compared with a field control sample over 0 <= z <= 6. Analysis of galaxy and SMBH demographics, AGN fractions, bolometric luminosity functions, and SMBH accretion rate density under homogeneous selection criteria.
AI.result: Protoclusters host systematically more massive galaxies and SMBHs than the field (up to 1 dex) at all redshifts, with accelerated evolution visible at z~3-4. AGN fraction increases with stellar mass similarly in both environments; at fixed stellar mass it is broadly consistent, indicating no strong environmental triggering. Yet protoclusters show a >2x AGN activity enhancement versus redshift, especially at high luminosity and early times. Protoclusters dominate the bright end of the AGN bolometric luminosity function and contribute up to ~50% of total SMBH accretion rate density at z~6.
AI.conclusion: The AGN enhancement in protoclusters primarily stems from differences in stellar-mass distributions—massive systems assemble earlier in overdense regions—rather than from direct environmental triggering of SMBH accretion.

title: Connecting Dynamo Theory with DNS Data: A Computational Analysis of α and \b{eta} Effects
comment: 26p, IDL analysis code in Appendix
summary: We investigate the influence of current helicity on the turbulent magnetic diffusivity $β$ using three complementary derivations of the $α$ and $β$ coefficients, based on the large-scale magnetic field $\overline{\mathbf{B}}$, the turbulent velocity $\mathbf{u}$, and the turbulent magnetic field $\mathbf{b}$. Applying these coefficients to raw DNS data, we reconstruct $\overline{\mathbf{B}}$ and compare the results with the original simulations. In the kinematic regime all models agree well with the DNS data. In the nonlinear regime, however, $β_{\mathrm{vv-vw}}$ alone produces unbounded growth of $\overline{\mathbf{B}}$. Including the contribution from turbulent magnetic fields ($β_{\mathrm{bb+jb}}$) suppresses this unphysical growth and restores agreement with the DNS results. We find that kinetic helicity drives $β$ more negative, while current helicity shifts it back toward zero. Weighted combinations of the coefficients further show that the $β$ effect dominates the evolution of $\overline{\mathbf{B}}$ throughout, whereas the $α$ effect becomes important mainly for sustaining the field in the nonlinear regime. The corresponding IDL analysis scripts are provided to facilitate practical implementation of the theoretical models.

AI.tldr: Three derivations of the α and β turbulent transport coefficients are compared against DNS data; current helicity in β_{\mathrm{bb+jb}} is essential to suppress unphysical growth of the mean field in the nonlinear regime.
AI.motivation: The turbulent magnetic diffusivity β is a key closure parameter in mean-field dynamo theory, yet different derivations yield differing expressions and their validity in the nonlinear (saturated) regime is unclear. The paper aims to clarify which contributions to β are required for mean-field models to reproduce direct numerical simulations.
AI.method: Three complementary derivations of the α and β coefficients are obtained from large-scale magnetic field B̄, turbulent velocity u, and turbulent magnetic field b. These coefficients are computed from raw DNS data and used to reconstruct B̄, whose evolution is compared with the original simulations, in both the kinematic and nonlinear regimes. Weighted combinations of the coefficients are also tested, and IDL analysis scripts are released.
AI.result: In the kinematic regime all models agree with the DNS. In the nonlinear regime, β_{vv-vw} alone gives unbounded growth of B̄. Adding the turbulent-magnetic-field contribution (β_{bb+jb}) removes this unphysical growth and recovers agreement with the DNS. Kinetic helicity drives β more negative, while current helicity shifts it back toward zero. Weighted combinations show β dominates the evolution of B̄ throughout, with α becoming important mainly for sustaining the field nonlinearly.
AI.conclusion: Accurate nonlinear mean-field modeling requires including the current-helicity (turbulent magnetic field) contribution to β, particularly via β_{bb+jb}, to avoid spurious unbounded growth. The β effect controls the overall evolution of B̄, while α mainly sustains the field in the saturated state.

title: Little Dots: the ULX Analogy
comment: MNRAS, accepted
summary:
I consider recent observations of the Little Dots (LDs) observed in high--redshift ($z\sim 7$) galaxies. I have suggested that the central black holes in these objects are probably fed mass at very super--Eddington (factors $\sim 50$) rates. In physical terms, this idea makes them supermassive analogues of the (stellar--mass) ultraluminous X--ray sources (ULXs), whose hard X--ray emission is strongly anisotropic (`beamed').
  In this paper I argue that the recent discovery of extended rest--frame hard X--ray ionization cones from an LD gives strong quantitative support to this view, as its geometry is what one would expect from a ULX--like object viewed not along one of its X--ray beams, but instead `from the side', very similar to the extreme Galactic system SS433. This in turn agrees in quantitative terms with recent suggestions that LDs resemble supermassive versions of SS433--like systems.
  I emphasize that in contrast, the rest--frame {\it soft} X--ray emission from LDs must be roughly {\it isotropic}, and presumably power the torus emission observed from these galaxies.

AI.tldr: The extended hard X-ray ionization cones recently observed in a Little Dot support the idea that Little Dots are supermassive, ULX-like systems with beamed emission viewed from the side, akin to a supermassive SS433.
AI.motivation: Recent observations of Little Dots in high-redshift (z~7) galaxies raise the question of how their central black holes are fueled. The author previously proposed that these black holes accrete at very super-Eddington rates (factors ~50), making them supermassive analogues of stellar-mass ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs), whose hard X-ray emission is strongly anisotropic (beamed).
AI.method: The author analyzes the recent discovery of extended rest-frame hard X-ray ionization cones from a Little Dot and interprets their geometry quantitatively, comparing it with the expected appearance of a ULX-like object viewed from the side rather than along an X-ray beam, analogous to the Galactic system SS433.
AI.result: The geometry of the extended hard X-ray ionization cones agrees quantitatively with what is expected for a ULX-like, beamed emitter observed off-axis, supporting the view that Little Dots resemble supermassive versions of SS433-like systems.
AI.conclusion: The extended hard X-ray ionization cones provide strong quantitative support for the super-Eddington, ULX-like interpretation of Little Dots. The author emphasizes that, in contrast to the beamed hard X-ray emission, the rest-frame soft X-ray emission from Little Dots must be roughly isotropic and presumably powers the torus emission observed from these galaxies.

title: The changing optical and X-ray emission of the dormant $γ$ Cas star HD 45314
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: $γ$ Cas stars are Oe/Be stars that exhibit bright and hard X-ray emission. HD45314 belonged to this category, but lost its $γ$ Cas characteristics as its circumstellar disc started to fade away. The star was monitored in optical spectroscopy, optical photometry, and X-ray spectroscopy to follow its variability on timescales of hours to years. Time series of magnitudes, colours, line equivalent widths and violet over red peak intensity ratios were analysed with Fourier methods to uncover possible periodicities. For five years, HD45314 exhibited oscillations of its magnitude and line strengths on a timescale of 230 d. It then declined towards a nearly disc-free stage and is now slowly rebuilding its disc. During these phases, the violet over red peak intensity ratio exhibited a modulation on a timescale of about 1190 d. Over the whole campaign, prominent short-term photometric variations, notably at a frequency of 3.369 d$^{-1}$, were probably due to $β$ Cep-type pulsations. The amplitude of these pulsations was stronger during phases of overall brightness changes. In parallel, the X-ray spectrum switched to a low state at the onset of the oscillation phase and has remained in this low state since then. Some residual hard emission is nonetheless observed. HD45314's long-term optical variations bear resemblance with the predictions of smooth particle hydrodynamics calculations, although a close look does reveal some inconsistencies. Unlike some other $γ$ Cas stars, where the X-ray emission remained nearly constant despite major changes of the circumstellar disc, HD45314's X-ray properties changed dramatically as the disc begun to dissipate. These differences might arise from a wider orbital separation between the Oe star and its putative white dwarf companion or from the ablation of the disc by the radiation field of the Oe star.

AI.tldr: HD45314, a former γ Cas star, was monitored via optical spectroscopy, photometry, and X-ray spectroscopy over hours-to-years timescales; its disc faded and rebuilt while multiple periodicities and a dramatic X-ray state change were observed.
AI.motivation: γ Cas stars are Oe/Be stars with bright, hard X-ray emission, and HD45314 was one such object until its circumstellar disc began to dissipate. The work aims to follow the star's variability across optical and X-ray bands to understand how disc evolution couples to X-ray behaviour and pulsation activity.
AI.method: Optical spectroscopy, optical photometry, and X-ray spectroscopy were used to monitor the star over hours to years. Time series of magnitudes, colours, line equivalent widths, and violet-over-red peak intensity ratios were analysed with Fourier methods to search for periodicities and characterize variability.
AI.result: HD45314 showed 230 d oscillations of magnitude and line strengths for five years, after which it declined to a nearly disc-free stage and is now slowly rebuilding its disc. The violet-over-red peak intensity ratio was modulated on ~1190 d. Prominent short-term photometric variations, notably at 3.369 d⁻¹, were likely β Cep-type pulsations, stronger during overall brightness changes. The X-ray spectrum switched to a low state at the onset of the oscillation phase and has remained low, with some residual hard emission. Long-term optical variations resemble smooth particle hydrodynamics predictions, though with some inconsistencies.
AI.conclusion: Unlike other γ Cas stars whose X-ray emission stayed nearly constant despite major disc changes, HD45314's X-ray properties changed dramatically as the disc dissipated. These differences may arise from a wider orbital separation between the Oe star and its putative white dwarf companion, or from ablation of the disc by the Oe star's radiation field.

title: TDCOSMO XXX: Spatially resolved kinematics of the deflectors in time-delay lens systems B1608+656 and SDSSJ1206+4332 from JWST-NIRSpec observation
comment: 22 pages, 10 figures, 3 tables; submitted to PRD
summary: We present spatially resolved stellar kinematics of the deflector galaxies in two time-delay lens systems, B1608+656 and SDSS J1206+4332, measured from JWST NIRSpec integral field spectroscopy. B1608+656 is a quadruply imaged quasar lensed by a pair of tidally interacting galaxies, the primary deflector (G1) and a close companion (G2), for which we quantified G2's tidal influence on G1 and define a criterion identifying the region where this perturbation is negligible and standard Jeans-equation modeling remains valid. SDSS J1206+4332 is a doubly imaged quasar whose extended host galaxy is itself quadruply imaged by a foreground massive galaxy (G0), accompanied by a fainter perturber (G1). For both systems, we report the first spectroscopic redshift and velocity dispersion measurements of the perturber galaxies. For G2 in B1608+656, we measure σ_v = 188 +/- 7 (stat.) +/- 2 (sys.) km/s at z = 0.6307, identical to the redshift of the main deflector G1. For G1 in SDSS J1206+4332, we find σ_v = 100 +/- 21 (stat.) +/- 2 (sys.) km/s at z = 0.7403, slightly lower than the primary deflector G0. The resolved velocity maps of both primary deflectors show clear rotation signatures and we visually classify them as fast or regular rotators. The data products will be made publicly available and will be combined with time delays, lens models, and line-of-sight convergence to measure cosmological parameters in the upcoming TDCOSMO 2026 milestone publication.

AI.tldr: We measure spatially resolved stellar kinematics of deflector galaxies in the lens systems B1608+656 and SDSS J1206+4332 using JWST NIRSpec IFU data, reporting the first spectroscopic redshifts and velocity dispersions for their perturber galaxies, and characterizing the primary deflectors as fast/regular rotators for use in future cosmographic analyses.
AI.motivation: Time-delay lens systems are powerful cosmological probes, but their accuracy depends on modeling the deflector mass distribution, which requires stellar kinematics. Perturber galaxies near the primary deflector can bias standard Jeans-equation modeling, so spatially resolved kinematics of both primary and perturber galaxies are needed to validate modeling assumptions and improve cosmological constraints.
AI.method: JWST NIRSpec integral field spectroscopy was used to obtain spatially resolved stellar kinematics of deflector galaxies in two time-delay lenses, B1608+656 (quadruple quasar lensed by interacting pair G1 and G2) and SDSS J1206+4332 (double quasar with quadruply imaged host lensed by G0 plus perturber G1). The tidal influence of G2 on G1 was quantified, and a criterion was defined for the region where this perturbation is negligible and standard Jeans-equation modeling remains valid.
AI.result: For G2 in B1608+656, σ_v = 188 ± 7 (stat.) ± 2 (sys.) km/s at z = 0.6307, identical to the main deflector G1. For G1 in SDSS J1206+4332, σ_v = 100 ± 21 (stat.) ± 2 (sys.) km/s at z = 0.7403, slightly lower than the primary deflector G0. These are the first spectroscopic redshifts and velocity dispersions measured for the perturber galaxies. The resolved velocity maps of both primary deflectors show clear rotation signatures, visually classified as fast or regular rotators.
AI.conclusion: The data products will be made publicly available and combined with time delays, lens models, and line-of-sight convergence to measure cosmological parameters in the upcoming TDCOSMO 2026 milestone publication.

title: Validity of the CRD limit for modeling scattering polarization in the photospheric Sr I 4607 Å line
summary: Context. Scattering polarization in the Sr I 4607 Å line is a key diagnostic for small-scale, unresolved magnetic fields in the quiet solar photosphere, inaccessible to Zeeman-based techniques. The complete frequency redistribution (CRD) limit is commonly used to model this line, but its validity and impact on magnetic sensitivity have not been systematically investigated. This is timely given new facilities observing this line with unprecedented accuracy, and future synoptic programs targeting long-term quiet-Sun magnetism. Aims. We assess the CRD limit against the general partial frequency redistribution (PRD) description of scattering for the Sr I 4607 Å polarization, focusing on its magnetic sensitivity via the Hanle effect. Methods. We solved the non-LTE radiative transfer problem for polarized radiation in a semi-empirical 1D plane-parallel static atmosphere, with CRD and PRD scattering, across magnetic field configurations relevant for Hanle diagnostics. Results. For small-scale unresolved fields, where the field acts only via Hanle depolarization of Q/I, CRD and PRD emergent profiles and Hanle sensitivity are essentially identical. For deterministic fields, CRD remains accurate when polarization signals exceed about 0.3%; for weaker signals, PRD effects can appreciably affect the emergent profiles. Conclusions. CRD is adequate for modeling Sr I 4607 Å scattering polarization in the vast majority of observationally relevant cases; PRD effects matter only for weak polarization signals.

AI.tldr: The CRD limit for modeling Sr I 4607 Å scattering polarization is validated against full PRD, showing the two are essentially identical for Hanle depolarization by unresolved fields, with PRD effects appearing only for weak polarization signals below ~0.3%.
AI.motivation: Scattering polarization in Sr I 4607 Å is a key diagnostic of small-scale unresolved magnetic fields in the quiet solar photosphere, but its modeling typically relies on the CRD limit whose validity and impact on magnetic (Hanle) sensitivity have not been systematically investigated. This assessment is timely given new high-accuracy observing facilities and future quiet-Sun synoptic programs.
AI.method: Non-LTE radiative transfer for polarized radiation was solved in a semi-empirical 1D plane-parallel static atmosphere, comparing CRD and PRD scattering across magnetic field configurations relevant to Hanle diagnostics.
AI.result: For unresolved small-scale fields (Hanle depolarization of Q/I only), CRD and PRD emergent profiles and Hanle sensitivity are essentially identical. For deterministic fields, CRD stays accurate when polarization signals exceed ~0.3%; below this level, PRD effects appreciably alter emergent profiles.
AI.conclusion: CRD is adequate for modeling Sr I 4607 Å scattering polarization in the vast majority of observationally relevant cases, with PRD effects mattering only for weak polarization signals.

title: Characterization of Orbits in Bars in Disc Galaxies Using Fourier Frequencies
comment: 19 pages, 23 figures, accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: Bars are among the most prominent dynamical structures in disc galaxies, yet their long-term evolution and the orbital families that sustain them remain only partially understood. In this work, we introduce a new methodology based on frozen potentials combined with Fourier analysis of particle trajectories to identify regular and sticky orbits in self-consistent $N$-body simulations. This approach allows us to isolate particles belonging to the $x_1$ family, directly associated with the bar, and the $x_2$ family, linked to a secondary perpendicular structure. Tracking these orbits across multiple snapshots enables us to quantify the time evolution of key bar properties, including its mass fraction, semi-axes, and density profile. Compared with established used diagnostics, our method provides the closest match to the temporal behaviour of the Fourier bar-strength parameter $A_2$, while offering a direct dynamical interpretation and full three-dimensional characterization that Fourier-based approaches cannot provide. Our analysis further reveals that the indices $n_x$, $n_y$, and $n_z$ describing the bar density distribution are anisotropic and rarely equal to the canonical $n=2$ assumed in Ferrers profiles, highlighting the limitations of standard analytical approximations. We also find strong correlations between bar growth, orbital chaoticity, and angular momentum redistribution, with the bar acting both as a sink and as a driver of angular momentum transfer. A comparison between the two models analysed shows that rapidly forming bars are weaker and less stable than those that grow more gradually. Altogether, our methodology provides a robust framework for linking orbital structure to the dynamical evolution of barred galaxies.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a frozen-potential plus Fourier-trajectory method to classify regular and sticky orbits in self-consistent N-body simulations, isolating x1 (bar) and x2 (secondary perpendicular) families, tracking bar properties over time, and linking bar growth to orbital chaoticity and angular-momentum redistribution.
AI.motivation: Bars are prominent dynamical structures in disc galaxies, but their long-term evolution and the orbital families sustaining them are only partially understood. Established Fourier-based diagnostics of bar strength lack direct dynamical interpretation and full 3D characterization.
AI.method: A new methodology combining frozen potentials with Fourier analysis of particle trajectories to identify regular and sticky orbits in self-consistent N-body simulations. Particles in the x1 (bar) and x2 (secondary perpendicular structure) families are isolated, and their orbits are tracked across multiple snapshots to quantify the time evolution of bar mass fraction, semi-axes, and density profile.
AI.result: The method best matches the temporal behaviour of the Fourier bar-strength parameter A2 compared with established diagnostics, while providing direct dynamical interpretation and full 3D characterization. The density-profile indices nx, ny, nz are anisotropic and rarely equal to the canonical n=2 of Ferrers profiles. Strong correlations are found between bar growth, orbital chaoticity, and angular-momentum redistribution, with the bar acting both as sink and driver. Rapidly forming bars are weaker and less stable than gradually growing ones.
AI.conclusion: The methodology offers a robust framework linking orbital structure to the dynamical evolution of barred galaxies, and highlights the limitations of standard analytical (e.g., Ferrers) approximations for bar density distributions.

title: Studies of Two Post Common Envelope Binary Stars
comment: Accepted to MNRAS, 16 pages, 14 figures
summary: New time series photometry of the short period ($P<0.2$~d) binary stars ZTF~J032906.36+070408.3 (ZTF~0329) and ATO~J090.7238+00.5996 (ATL~0602) is presented. The primary (hotter) stars in both systems are white dwarfs, while the cooler stars are M dwarfs. Archival photometry and new and archival spectra are used to derive the temperatures of the components in the two binaries. Both are single-lined binaries. Velocity curves are fitted to radial velocity measurements of the red dwarfs and used to place lower limits on the masses of the white dwarfs. New and archival time series photometry show evolution in the shapes of the light curves of both stars. Spectra of ZTF~0329 show an excess of radiation in the $R_C$ band which is ascribed to electron cyclotron radiation, suggesting that the star is a low accretion rate polar. Satisfactory model fits to the multi-filter light curves of ATL~0602 require the presence of cool spots on the red component of the binary. The latter star exhibits a variety of velocities associated with Balmer and Ca~II emission lines within individual spectra.

AI.tldr: New and archival photometry plus spectroscopy of two short-period (P<0.2 d) binaries, ZTF 0329 and ATL 0602, reveal white dwarf + M dwarf single-lined systems, with ZTF 0329 likely a low accretion rate polar and ATL 0602 showing starspots and complex emission-line velocities.
AI.motivation: Short-period white dwarf + M dwarf binaries are important for understanding binary evolution, mass transfer, and accretion processes. The study characterizes two such newly identified systems, ZTF J032906.36+070408.3 and ATO J090.7238+00.5996, to constrain their component properties and interaction mechanisms.
AI.method: Combined new time-series photometry with archival photometry and new/archival spectra. Component temperatures were derived for both binaries. Radial velocity curves of the red (M) dwarfs were fitted to set lower limits on the white dwarf masses. Multi-filter light curves were modeled, and emission-line velocity behavior was examined.
AI.result: Both systems are single-lined binaries with a hotter white dwarf primary and cooler M dwarf secondary. Light curve shapes evolve over time for both stars. ZTF 0329 shows R_C-band excess attributed to electron cyclotron radiation, indicating a low accretion rate polar. ATL 0602 requires cool spots on the red component for satisfactory multi-filter fits, and displays a variety of Balmer and Ca II emission-line velocities within individual spectra. Lower limits on the white dwarf masses were obtained.
AI.conclusion: The two short-period binaries are single-lined white dwarf + M dwarf systems. ZTF 0329 is likely a low accretion rate polar, while ATL 0602 is a spotted, magnetically active system with complex emission-line kinematics, highlighting diversity among short-period white dwarf binaries.

title: JWST Spectra Conclusively Show an Excess of Neutral Gas Outflows in Quiescent Galaxies at z=2-5
comment: 30 pages, 12 figures, 9 tables; submitted to ApJ
summary: Galaxies exhibit a broad range of star formation activity, from actively star-forming to quiescent systems. Yet, the mechanisms responsible for the rapid shutdown and continued suppression of star formation remain poorly understood, particularly for the quiescent galaxies recently uncovered by JWST at $z>3$. Neutral gas outflows provide a direct tracer of gas removal and regulation in quiescent galaxies. We therefore present a NaID $λ\lambda5891,5897$ absorption--line stacking analysis of 274 galaxies at $z=2$--5 drawn from the DAWN JWST Archive (DJA) and the EMBER JWST program, using JWST/NIRSpec medium-resolution grating spectroscopy and NIRCam photometry. NaID absorption is detected in all quiescent galaxy stacks spanning $z=2$--5, providing the first statistical evidence that neutral gas outflows are a ubiquitous feature of quiescent galaxies in the early Universe. Compared to the non-quiescent galaxy stacks, the quiescent stacks show mass loading factors higher by 2--4 dex, with mass outflow rates $\dot{M}_{\rm out} \sim 9$--$30\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$ elevated by $\sim0.5$--$1$ dex and outflow velocities $v_{\rm out} \sim 310$--$570\,{\rm km\,s}^{-1}$ higher by a factor of $\sim2$. The extreme mass loading factor values and declining star formation histories strongly indicate that these outflows cannot be driven by current star formation alone. In the statistically reliable quiescent redshift bins at $2 \leq z < 3$ and $3 \leq z < 4$, the elevated $[\mathrm{N\,II}]/\mathrm{H}α$ and $[\mathrm{O\,III}]/\mathrm{H}β$ ratios are consistent with a possible AGN contribution, suggesting that non-stellar feedback may play a role in sustaining quiescence in galaxies at these epochs.

AI.tldr: A NaID absorption-line stacking analysis of 274 galaxies at z=2–5 reveals ubiquitous neutral gas outflows in quiescent galaxies, with extreme mass loading factors and outflow rates suggesting non-stellar (possibly AGN) feedback drives and sustains their quiescence.
AI.motivation: The mechanisms responsible for the rapid shutdown and continued suppression of star formation remain poorly understood, especially for the quiescent galaxies recently uncovered by JWST at z>3. Neutral gas outflows offer a direct tracer of gas removal and regulation, yet their role in early-universe quiescent galaxies has lacked statistical characterization.
AI.method: The authors performed a NaID λλ5891,5897 absorption-line stacking analysis of 274 galaxies at z=2–5 drawn from the DAWN JWST Archive (DJA) and the EMBER JWST program, using JWST/NIRSpec medium-resolution grating spectroscopy and NIRCam photometry.
